market_brief: Huang's reinstatement turned Monday's bounce into a squeeze: the S&P 500 rose 4.7% to 7,237, the Nasdaq 100 6.9% and the SOX 14% as Nvidia closed up 31%, MSCI EM gained 7.4% and the VIX fell 26% to 26.6. Asia is following on Tuesday, with the Kospi up nearly 6% (briefly above 5,000), the Nikkei up about 4% after its holiday and the ASX up 1.4%. India stays shut for Guru Nanak Jayanti after Monday's 1.75% Nifty drop. The rally comes with hawkish rates: after Williams, a December Fed hike is fully priced and January odds are about 67%, the 2-year rose about 7bp to around 4.69% while the 10-year was flat at 4.92%, and the DXY rose 0.5% to 104.3. Commodities split: Brent fell 6.2% to $86.8 and WTI 4.4% to $80.3 on returning supply, while gold rose 3.2% to $3,628 and silver 4.5%. Bitcoin was flat near $61k as ETF outflows continue. Dell reports Tuesday after the close, with PCE and GDP due Wednesday.
ai_brief: Compute and capital lead the AI news: Amazon confirmed its Decart deal to push Trainium, xAI is reportedly renting most of its compute to Anthropic and Google, and Sierra doubled its valuation to $30bn. On products, coding agents moved further with Anthropic's Claude Ship (auto-approved PRs) and GPT-6.2 Sol becoming ChatGPT's default. Policy pressure is building, with Altman backing shared development limits and a House panel disclosing about 879k AI-chip licenses approved for China.

items.headline: Update: Nvidia closes up 31% after Huang is reinstated as CEO; Nasdaq has best day since April 2025
items.summary: Monday's pre-market bounce turned into a full-session rally once the board confirmed Huang's return. Nvidia added nearly $1tn in market value, the SOX rose about 14%, the Nasdaq 100 6.9% and the S&P 500 4.7% to 7,237, and the VIX fell to about 26.6.

items.headline: Update: December Fed hike now fully priced after Williams; odds of a January hike jump to 67%
items.summary: NY Fed's Williams said inflation is still too high and may stay above 2% until 2028, keeping further hikes on the table. Per Reuters, CME pricing for a 25bp December hike rose to 100% from about 89% on Friday, and a 50bp move has been priced out.

items.headline: Kospi jumps nearly 6% and briefly tops 5,000, triggering a buy-side sidecar
items.summary: This reverses Monday's 3.3% drop. Samsung Electronics rose about 7% and SK Hynix about 8.5% in early Tuesday trade. Program buying was paused for five minutes, and foreigners were net buyers.

items.headline: Nikkei reopens up nearly 4% after Monday's holiday, trading around 58,600
items.summary: This is Tokyo's first session since Huang's return. Kioxia rose about 6.6% and SoftBank Group about 5% in early trade. The latest.json Nikkei print is still Friday's close.

items.headline: Brokers reverse Nvidia downgrades: Melius, Bernstein, Oppenheimer and StoneX upgrade
items.summary: Melius moved to buy with a $220 target, and Bernstein went back to outperform with a $200 target. Oppenheimer and StoneX also upgraded, and Citi raised its target to $240.

items.headline: HPE beats, guides FY27 well above consensus and adds $5bn to its buyback, but shares slip after hours
items.summary: Q4 revenue was about $14.5bn and adjusted EPS $1.43 against $1.27 expected. FY27 guidance is $59.4–63.1bn revenue and $5.05–5.35 EPS. The stock fell roughly 5–7% after hours, reportedly on margin-mix worries, after rallying about 17% in the regular session.

items.headline: US flash services PMI misses at 54.7 as the 2-year yield rises about 7bp
items.summary: November flash services PMI came in at 54.7 against the 55.7 forecast, while manufacturing was in line at 54.5. The 2-year rose to about 4.69% while the 10-year ended near 4.92%, flattening the curve.

items.headline: Dollar near a 19-month high against the euro on Fed bets; yen around 159
items.summary: The dollar index rose about 0.5% to roughly 104.3, the euro slipped to about $1.09 and sterling to about $1.30. Hawkish Fed repricing and flows into US tech drove the moves, per Reuters.

items.headline: Oil falls to its lowest since late August as returning supply outweighs Gulf attacks
items.summary: Brent fell about 6% and WTI about 4% to around $80. Reports cited higher Middle East flows, the restart of Libya's Sharara pipeline, an IEA surplus call and Trump giving Iran diplomacy more time.

items.headline: STOXX 600 has its best day since May, up 1.9%, led by chipmakers
items.summary: Tech rose 4.7% after its worst week since March 2020, with AT&S, BE Semiconductor and Aixtron up 9–13%. Nemetschek fell 5.7% after a J.P. Morgan downgrade. The European prints in latest.json are still Friday's.

items.headline: S3 Partners: Nvidia shorts lost about $12bn on Monday; Stocktwits sentiment turns very bullish
items.summary: S3 estimates the rally erased about 90% of short sellers' gains from Nvidia's seven-day slide, and Nasdaq shorts lost about $39bn in total. In a Stocktwits poll, 64% of respondents said they felt more bullish.

items.headline: Questions remain after Nvidia's rebound: no public security finding, and a House interview on Dec 1
items.summary: The board reinstated Huang based on government assurances rather than a published finding. Huang still faces a closed-door House interview on December 1.

items.headline: TPG and Corpay to take BILL Holdings private for about $6bn
items.summary: Holders will get $63.25 a share in cash. Corpay invests $1.1bn for about a third of BILL and has an option to buy the rest in 2030. Starboard backs the deal.

items.headline: After-hours earnings: Agilent up about 7% on a beat; Zoom starts a dividend; Semtech falls
items.summary: Agilent guided FY27 above consensus. Zoom beat and declared its first $0.25 quarterly dividend, but a slightly soft Q4 guide nudged the stock lower. Semtech fell about 8% despite strong guidance as holders took profits.

items.headline: Tata Steel falls 8.4% on its APL Apollo deal of up to Rs 28,000 crore as Indian markets close for a holiday
items.summary: Tata Steel's stake purchase and asset swap weighed on metals, which fell 3.7% as Nifty closed 1.75% lower on Monday's moved-up expiry day. NSE and BSE are shut Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti and reopen Wednesday.

items.headline: Spot bitcoin ETFs shed $1.79bn in a week, the most since June
items.summary: It was the fourth straight week of outflows, led by IBIT. Ether ETFs have had eight weeks of outflows. Bitcoin missed the equity rally and is flat around $61k.

items.headline: ASX 200 rises 1.4% early, led by a 3.4% gain in tech
items.summary: WiseTech and NextDC rose about 4%, and materials gained as copper rebounded. Last week was the index's worst since 2022.

items.headline: Single-stock outliers: Capricor -75% on an FDA rejection; Oatly doubles on a tender offer
items.summary: Oatly's board advised holders not to accept Verlinvest's $4.13-per-ADS offer. Kymera launched a $1.5bn share sale, and Amentum authorised a buyback of up to $500m.

items.headline: Taiwan margin calls reportedly jumped about 200-fold during last week's AI selloff
items.summary: This points to forced retail deleveraging. Taiwan trades Tuesday after ASE and UMC ADRs rose about 20% in New York.

items.headline: Week ahead: Dell after Tuesday's close (whisper EPS about $7.25), Bank of Korea seen hiking to 3.25% Thursday, PCE and GDP Wednesday
items.summary: Dell consensus is about $6.60 EPS, and AI-server revenue and backlog conversion are the focus. In a Reuters poll, 32 of 34 economists expect the BoK to hike. US markets are closed Thursday, and India reopens Wednesday.

items.headline: Update: Amazon confirms deal for Decart's optimization tech and team as it readies Trainium sales
items.summary: What changed: the earlier 'nearing a deal' report is now an official announcement covering the Decart Optimization Stack and its founding team. The ~$7.5bn figure still comes from a Bloomberg report.

items.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Ship agents that review, fix and auto-approve pull requests
items.summary: The bundle includes Code Review (generally available), a PR Steward beta that fixes failing CI and merge conflicts, and an Approvals beta driven by plain-language policies. It is rolling out to Team and Enterprise plans on GitHub.

items.headline: Sierra raises $1.75bn at a $30bn valuation, doubling in six months
items.summary: Greenoaks and Lightspeed co-led the round for Bret Taylor's customer-service agent startup. Run-rate revenue reportedly doubled to $400m in five months.

items.headline: xAI reportedly shifts toward renting compute, with Anthropic its largest customer
items.summary: Per an NYT report summarised by The Decoder, Anthropic pays about $3.1bn a month and Google about $800m. Rentals reportedly make up more than half of xAI's revenue.

items.headline: GPT-6.2 Sol becomes ChatGPT's default chat model
items.summary: OpenAI is rolling out a chat-tuned GPT-6.2 Sol for paid tiers and says it improves handling of complex questions, search and images. The Work and Codex models are unchanged.

items.headline: Anthropic shares lag the AI rally as share unlocks loom
items.summary: ANT was roughly flat to slightly lower on Monday, below its $97 debut close but above its $83 IPO price. Needham flagged that up to 303m shares could unlock on Dec 15.

items.headline: House panel discloses about 879,000 AI-chip licenses approved for China; Commerce reportedly moves on Megaspeed
items.summary: Documents show Commerce approved H200 and MI325X licenses for Chinese firms from Dec 2025 to May 2026. Commerce is reportedly preparing to blacklist Singapore's Megaspeed.

items.headline: Update: Altman backs OpenAI's call for shared AI development limits
items.summary: What changed: Altman has endorsed Pachocki's proposal, per Bloomberg, and Pachocki warned AI could speed up its own development as early as 2027.

items.headline: Google Search AI Mode can now draw on Drive, Wallet and the Gemini app
items.summary: This is opt-in, and Wallet access is read-only. Context can also carry over between the Gemini app and AI Mode.

items.headline: Embo raises a $110m seed led by a16z for humanoid world models
items.summary: The team, which includes Dreamer creator Danijar Hafner, plans to pretrain on internet video and fine-tune on data from its own humanoid fleet. NVentures also invested.

items.headline: GPT-6.2 Astra reportedly writes the first Lean proof of a 2006 algebra theorem
items.summary: Vals AI says the model found its own proof route without human help. Astra leads Vals' Autoform-Hard benchmark.

items.headline: Governors seek a federal AI baseline; big banks reportedly restrict customer AI agents
items.summary: The NGA released bipartisan principles on frontier-model rules. Wired reports major banks have blocked or limited agents that log in with customer credentials.

items.headline: Trending: a Claude Code bug-hunting skill bundle and the Orca parallel-agent runner
items.summary: claude-bughunter added about 11k stars last week. Orca, which runs Claude Code and Codex agents in parallel worktrees, added about 7k.

items.headline: Google books a 2029 New Glenn launch for its Project Suncatcher orbital TPU test
items.summary: The plan is solar-powered satellites, each carrying roughly one data-center rack of TPUs. Cooling and reliability in orbit remain unproven.
